author: Hadir at-Tannus, scribe of Sentinel
pages:
West of Hammerfell the sea goes down and down, and then, if the divers of Stros M'Kai are to be believed, it comes up again in steps of cut stone.

The Ra Gada say their fathers came from a land that the sea swallowed. Most scholars smile at this. I no longer do.

Off the drowned coast I have seen courtyards under twenty fathoms of water, ringed by columns that a careless wave could not have built. Sand drifts through their doorways like the desert it once was.

In one such court a ring of green stone hangs in the water around a heart that glows.

Those who swim near it do not drown. I have felt it myself: the chest stops burning, the breath stops mattering. The divers call it the ward of the sea-temple and leave offerings of salt.

Whatever the Yokudans prayed to, something still listens down there.
